idiom_name: func value (or method value) passed to the callee
implementation_notes: Functions are first-class values, so the callback is a plain parameter or field of type func(...) and a closure or method value (h.handle) supplies the context - no interface or registration type is needed. For asynchronous completion the idiomatic replacement is a goroutine that sends its result on a channel, optionally selected against ctx.Done(): channels carry the value, the ordering and the cancellation, which a stored callback cannot. Keep the callback form where the API is inherently push-style (net/http handlers, sort.Slice's less function, hook and middleware registration lists) and the caller has no need to fan in or time out.
pitfalls: A callback that may never fire (cancelled context, error path that returns without calling) leaks the goroutine and whatever it holds; tie the operation to a context and make completion single-shot.
A nil func value panics when invoked, and a method value captures its receiver at evaluation time, so the receiver must stay valid and non-nil.
Invoking the callback while holding a mutex re-enters the callee through the callback; unlock before calling out.
Passing a method value keeps the receiver alive for the lifetime of the registration, which turns a listener list into a leak if entries are never removed.
